body.statement:
Fix \(M\ge2\), \(p\in(0,1)\), \(\rho\in(0,1]\), \(B\ge1\), and design sequences satisfying the three fraction and growth assumptions.  Put
\[
 d_{\mathrm{same}}=\frac1{Mp(1-p)},\qquad
 d_{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac1{Mp(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M},
\]
and suppose \(0<c_\sigma<d_{\mathrm{ind}}\).  There are high-prior-probability sets of deterministic Rademacher schedule rows whose Cartesian diagonal selections all belong to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\); after conditioning \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) on these sets, their induced one-realization mixture laws have total-variation distance tending to zero, while \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) converges uniformly on the respective supports to \(d_{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(d_{\mathrm{ind}}\).  Consequently there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every measurable \(\widehat S_n(\mathcal O_n)\) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}}
 \Pr_Y\left(\left|\frac{\widehat S_n}{\sigma_n^2}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \ge\frac12.
\]
Thus no estimator from one realization is uniformly ratio-consistent for the exact variance over the full dense class.  The deterministic support arrays, rather than a generally unavailable pair of deterministic arrays with close laws, are the valid diagonal certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(j\in\{\mathrm{same},\mathrm{ind}\}\), and write \(d_j\) for the corresponding constant in the theorem.  Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} gives
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}d_j                                     \tag{1}
\]
under \(\mathbb H_n^j\).  For \(t>0\), define the schedule-measurable conditional tail probability
\[
b_{n,t}(Y)=
\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>t\,\right|Y\right).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:rademacher-predictable-variation}, whose positive-density scope agrees with \(\rho\in(0,1]\), gives for each fixed integer \(k\geq1\)
\[
\mathbb H_n^j\{b_{n,1/k}(Y)>1/k\}\longrightarrow0.                   \tag{2}
\]
Set
\[
E_{n,k}^j=
\left\{Y:\ |G_n\sigma_n^2(Y)-d_j|\leq k^{-1},\quad
                 b_{n,1/k}(Y)\leq k^{-1}\right\}.                    \tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) imply \(\mathbb H_n^j(E_{n,k}^j)\to1\) for every fixed \(k\).

We record the elementary diagonal selection explicitly.  Choose increasing integers \(m_k\) such that, for both values of \(j\),
\[
n\geq m_k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathbb H_n^j(E_{n,k}^j)\geq1-k^{-1}.
\]
After increasing them if necessary, take \(m_{k+1}>m_k\).  For \(n\geq m_1\), define \(k_n=\max\{k:m_k\leq n\}\), while for \(n<m_1\) put \(k_n=1\).  Then \(k_n\to\infty\).  With
\[
\Gamma_n^j=
\begin{cases}
E_{n,k_n}^j,&n\geq m_1,\\
\operatorname{supp}(\mathbb H_n^j),&n<m_1,
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{4}
\]
we have \(\mathbb H_n^j(\Gamma_n^j)\to1\), and, for \(n\geq m_1\), uniformly on \(\Gamma_n^j\),
\[
|G_n\sigma_n^2(Y)-d_j|\leq k_n^{-1}.                                  \tag{5}
\]

Every schedule row in \(\Gamma_n^j\) is additive and satisfies \(|Y_{i,n}(z,A)|=1\leq B\).  The deterministic design sequences satisfy Assumptions~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, \ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction}, and \ref{ass:sampling-fraction}.  Since \(d_j>c_\sigma\), equation (5) implies the scaled-variance lower bound along every Cartesian selection \((Y_n)_{n\geq1}\in\prod_n\Gamma_n^j\).  Under the repaired Definition~\ref{def:dense-schedule-class}, these are exactly the remaining membership requirements, so every such selection belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\).

The construction has a stronger property that is not required for membership in the repaired ambient class.  For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), eventually \(k_n^{-1}<\varepsilon\), and (3)--(4) imply, for every \(Y_n\in\Gamma_n^j\),
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>\varepsilon\,\right|Y_n\right)
\leq b_{n,1/k_n}(Y_n)
\leq k_n^{-1}\longrightarrow0.                                       \tag{6}
\]
Thus the additive lower-bound supports satisfy predictable quadratic-variation stability by the construction-specific Lemma~\ref{lem:rademacher-predictable-variation}, even though \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) no longer assumes it.  This is the promised subclass certificate.

Let \(\widetilde{\mathbb H}_n^j\) be \(\mathbb H_n^j\) conditioned on \(\Gamma_n^j\), and let \(P_n^j\) be its image under the design-and-observation Markov kernel into \(\mathcal O_n\).  Conditioning changes a prior by total variation at most \(\mathbb H_n^j((\Gamma_n^j)^c)=o(1)\), and a Markov kernel contracts total variation.  Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} says that the two unconditioned observation mixtures are exactly equal.  The triangle inequality therefore yields
\[
\|P_n^{\mathrm{same}}-P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1).         \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=d_{\mathrm{same}}\), \(b=d_{\mathrm{ind}}\), and
\[
\Delta=a-b=2\rho/M>0.
\]
Choose \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta/(4a)\).  From (5), for all sufficiently large \(n\), the event
\[
\left|\widehat S_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|\leq\varepsilon                 \tag{8}
\]
implies
\[
G_n\widehat S_n>(a+b)/2
\quad\text{on }\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{same}},
\qquad
G_n\widehat S_n<(a+b)/2
\quad\text{on }\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.                               \tag{9}
\]
Indeed, as the uniform error in (5) tends to zero,
\[
(1-\varepsilon)(a-o(1))-(a+b)/2
\geq\Delta/2-\varepsilon a-o(1)>0,
\]
and
\[
(a+b)/2-(1+\varepsilon)(b+o(1))
\geq\Delta/2-\varepsilon a-o(1)>0.
\]

Use the measurable test that declares \(\mathrm{same}\) exactly when \(G_n\widehat S_n>(a+b)/2\).  By (8)--(9), the event that \(\widehat S_n\) has relative error at most \(\varepsilon\) implies correct classification under either conditioned prior.  Therefore the sum of testing-error probabilities is at most the sum of the two mixture probabilities of relative estimation error greater than \(\varepsilon\).

For completeness, if \(T_n\) is the test's \(\mathrm{same}\) decision set, then
\[
P_n^{\mathrm{same}}(T_n^c)+P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(T_n)
=1-P_n^{\mathrm{same}}(T_n)+P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(T_n)
\geq1-\|P_n^{\mathrm{same}}-P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Combining this inequality with (7) shows that the larger of the two mixture risks satisfies
\[
\max_{j\in\{\mathrm{same},\mathrm{ind}\}}
\int
\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.
\left|\widehat S_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|>\varepsilon
\right|Y\right)
\,d\widetilde{\mathbb H}_n^j(Y)
\geq\frac12-o(1).                                                     \tag{10}
\]

Each row in \(\Gamma_n^j\) can be extended to an infinite array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\): keep that row at index \(n\) and choose any member of \(\Gamma_m^j\) at every sufficiently large \(m\neq n\), with arbitrary bounded rows at the finitely many earlier indices.  The sets are nonempty eventually because their prior probabilities tend to one, and the resulting Cartesian selection obeys the deterministic fraction limits, the envelope, and, by (5), \(\liminf_mG_m\sigma_m^2=d_j>c_\sigma\).  Thus each average risk in (10) is bounded above by
\[
\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}}
\Pr_Y\left(\left|\frac{\widehat S_n}{\sigma_n^2}-1\right|
>\varepsilon\right).
\]
Taking the lower limit proves the asserted lower bound \(1/2\).  The support schedules are additive and have no composition interference, and hence form a subclass of the arbitrary bounded composition-interference schedules.  The impossibility on this subclass therefore transfers upward to the entire repaired ambient class.
body.justification: Equal observed-data mixtures with two uniformly separated scaled variance limits yield an all-statistic testing lower bound after conditioning on high-probability deterministic support sets.  Its concrete negative target is the one-realization equal-group CR2 workflow implemented by \({\tt clubSandwich::vcovCR}({\tt type}={\tt 'CR2'})\): PustejovskyTipton2018, Theorem 1, gives that workflow exact unbiasedness only under its specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
body.gap: PustejovskyTipton2018, Theorem 1, does not claim exact recovery under finite-pool random-partition dependence: its exact-unbiasedness scope is a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.  This theorem leaves that scope intact, but rules out extending the same one-realization CR2 workflow—or any observed-data correction—to uniformly ratio-consistent recovery of the exact dense-PAME design variance.  The lower bound is established on additive no-interference schedules; because this is a subclass of arbitrary bounded composition interference, it transfers upward to the full ambient class.
body.consumer: For the precise \({\tt clubSandwich}\) equal-group consumer, the result says that a single realized-partition CR2 output may be reported as the conservative procedure characterized above, but cannot be promoted to a uniformly exact design-variance correction at positive density without added structure, repeated regrouping, or a bound.  Its witness supports separately satisfy predictable-variation stability even though the repaired ambient class does not require it.
